reason: E1 supports L12 precipitation in the fcc phase and Orowan strengthening, but it does not show that precipitates form preferentially along lamellar interfaces, nor does it provide evidence that such precipitation reduces dislocation pile-ups, stress concentrations, or brittleness. The key mechanistic premise linking L12 to ductility improvement via pile-up reduction is unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Low-temperature aging of Al0.7CoCrFeNi precipitates coherent L12 nanoparticles in the fcc phase.
These L12 precipitates strengthen the alloy via an Orowan dislocation bowing/bypass mechanism.
The alloy has a lamellar dual-phase (fcc+B2) microstructure with many fcc-bcc interfaces.
Dislocation pile-ups at internal boundaries cause local stress concentrations, microcracking, and brittleness in the untreated alloy.
Distributing L12 precipitates along lamellar interfaces will reduce dislocation pile-ups and improve ductility.
